# REQ-2283: Generator and analyzer crash with IndexOutOfRangeException on a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2283

#### Bug description

Both `MessagePackGenerator` (CS8785) and `MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer` (AD0001) throw `IndexOutOfRangeException` when a `[MessagePackObject]` type has a member whose type is a **closed generic value type defined in a referenced assembly**.

Because the generator then "will not contribute to the output", the compiling assembly silently ends up with **no generated resolver at all**. It is only a warning, so a normal build looks fine, but trimmed and NativeAOT apps fail at runtime. In our case three assemblies of a large app had been shipping without a resolver across two releases before we noticed.

#### Repro steps

Two projects. `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack;
namespace Lib;

[MessagePackObject]
public partial record struct Item<T>([property: Key(0)] string Key);
```

`app`, with a `ProjectReference` to `lib`:

```csharp
using MessagePack; using Lib;
namespace App;

[MessagePackObject]
public sealed partial record Cmd([property: Key(0)] string Scope)
{
    [Key(1)] public Item<int> Member { get; init; }
}
```

Then `dotnet build` on `app`. Both projects are in the attached `mp-repro.zip`.

#### Expected behavior

A clean build, with a generated resolver in `app`.
#### Actual behavior

```
CSC : warning CS8785: Generator 'MessagePackGenerator' failed to generate source. It will not
contribute to the output and compilation errors may occur as a result. Exception was of type
'IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the bounds of the array.'.
CSC : warning AD0001: Analyzer 'MessagePack.SourceGenerator.Analyzers.MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer'
threw an exception of type 'System.IndexOutOfRangeException' with message 'Index was outside the
bounds of the array.'.
```

`app.dll` contains no `GeneratedMessagePackResolver`.

- Version used: MessagePack 3.1.8
- Runtime: .NET 10 (SDK 10.0.204), Windows 11

#### Additional context

**What triggers it.** `Item` is declared in `lib`, `Cmd` in `app`:

| `Item` declared as | result |
|---|---|
| `record struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item<T>` | **crash** |
| `struct Item` | ok |
| `record struct Item` | ok |
| `class Item<T>` | ok |
| `record class Item<T>` | ok |

So it needs all three of: **generic**, **value type**, **from a referenced assembly**. Moving the identical `Item<T>` declaration into `app` itself makes the crash disappear, which is what makes this specific to metadata symbols.
**Stack trace.**

```
System.IndexOutOfRangeException: Index was outside the bounds of the array.
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol)
   at TypeCollector.CollectGeneric(INamedTypeSymbol type, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 661
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 371
   at TypeCollector.GetObjectInfo(INamedTypeSymbol formattedType, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 1062
   at TypeCollector.CollectCore(ITypeSymbol typeSymbol, ISymbol callerSymbol) in TypeCollector.cs:line 386
   at TypeCollector.Collect() in TypeCollector.cs:line 300
   at MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.AnalyzeSymbol(SymbolAnalysisContext, ReferenceSymbols, AnalyzerOptions) in MsgPack00xMessagePackAnalyzer.cs:line 431
```

`CollectGeneric` line 661 is the closed-generic branch that calls `GetObjectInfo` directly:

```csharp
else
{
    // NOTE: ... closed generic types such as `Foo<string>` are not registered as a formatter.
    this.GetObjectInfo(type, callerSymbol);
```

so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax. Several diagnostic paths inside it index `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` directly (lines 735, 1009, 1101) instead of using `FirstOrDefault()` the way the neighbouring `GetIdentifierLocation` / `GetLocation` / `GetParameterListLocation` helpers already do, and that collection is empty for a metadata symbol. I did not narrow down which of the three fires.

**Getting the stack trace.** Console output truncates the exception to its message; `-p:ErrorLog=out.sarif` preserves the full description, including the stack trace and an `ISymbol:` context line naming the offending type:

```
dotnet build -p:ErrorLog=out.sarif
```

**Workaround.** Putting `[MessagePackFormatter(typeof(ItemFormatter<>))]` on the generic value type short-circuits `CollectCore` (line 356) before `GetObjectInfo` is reached, at the cost of hand-writing the formatter.

**Possibly related:** #2092 reports CS8785 from the v3 generator, but with a different inner exception and no repro.

story.summary: Stops the source generator and the MsgPack00x analyzer from crashing when a [MessagePackObject] member's type is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly. Two diagnostic sites that read `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` now tolerate an empty collection. TypeCollector's diagnostic callback is wrapped in a filter meant to drop diagnostics with no location in the current compilation. Three tests compile a defining assembly to a metadata-only image, run the analyzers and generator against a consuming project, and assert there are no diagnostics and that the resolver is generated. README and MsgPack004.md gain notes about types from referenced assemblies.
story.why: REQ-2283: an IndexOutOfRangeException in GetObjectInfo on metadata symbols made the generator drop the whole resolver (CS8785) and the analyzer fail (AD0001).
touches_beyond_requirement: A global filter on every diagnostic TypeCollector reports, not just the crashing sites. Any diagnostic without a source location is now silently dropped.
A policy decision to suppress member diagnostics for referenced types, documented as user-facing behaviour in README and MsgPack004.md.
story.confidence_overview: Medium. The two patched sites clearly no longer index an empty array. The tests reproduce the issue's record-struct case and a plain generic struct. The issue names three indexing sites; only two appear in the diff, and the third (issue line 735) is untouched. The filter's condition uses `||`, which does not do what its doc comment says. The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull path is not exercised by any test. I could not confirm the new tests fail without the fix.

claims.text: The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull diagnostic now uses the new GetPropertyIdentifierLocation helper. The helper returns null when the property has no PropertyDeclarationSyntax, instead of indexing [0] and hard-casting.

claims.text: README gains a section saying closed generic types from referenced assemblies are supported as members and that their member diagnostics are reported by the defining assembly.
MsgPack004.md gains a section saying the analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled.
TypeCollector's constructor wraps the non-null analyzer diagnostic callback so that every reported diagnostic goes through ReportIfLocatedInCompilation; a null callback stays null.

ReportIfLocatedInCompilation forwards a diagnostic only if its location is in source. Because of the `||`, any source location passes, including one in another compilation's tree. Metadata-located (Location.None) diagnostics are dropped.
claims.requirement_quote: so `GetObjectInfo` runs against a type that has no syntax.

claims.text: The MemberNeedsKey diagnostic now gets its location via `DeclaringSyntaxReferences.FirstOrDefault()?`, so a metadata member yields a null location instead of throwing IndexOutOfRangeException.

refusals.what: Global suppression of every TypeCollector diagnostic that lacks a source location.
refusals.why: This goes beyond fixing the crash. It changes which analyzer diagnostics users see, which is a product decision the requirement did not ask for.

refusals.what: New user-facing docs committing to a diagnostics policy for referenced types.
refusals.why: These documentation promises are not required by the bug fix, and MsgPack004.md partly contradicts the implemented `||` check.

findings.description: The condition is `IsInSource || ContainsSyntaxTree(SourceTree)`. A non-source location has a null SourceTree, so the second clause can never be true when the first is false, and the check reduces to `IsInSource`. A source location in another compilation's tree (for example an IDE project reference, where referenced symbols are source symbols) is still reported, contrary to the doc comment. Analyzers may not do this, and Roslyn rejects it. `&&` was likely intended.

The issue lists three `DeclaringSyntaxReferences[0]` sites (old lines 735, 1009, 1101). Only the latter two appear in the diff; the first (around new line ~711) is unchanged. Arguments to `reportDiagnostic?.Invoke(...)` are evaluated whenever the analyzer callback is non-null, so that path may still throw IndexOutOfRangeException for metadata types on inputs the tests don't cover.

The wrapper silently drops every diagnostic whose location is not in source. Any diagnostic that previously used Location.None or a null location (for example from GetIdentifierLocation/GetLocation helpers on synthesized or metadata symbols) is now suppressed, not just those for referenced types. This may hide real problems.
The BothStringAndIntKeyAreNull change and GetPropertyIdentifierLocation are not exercised by any new test.

The doc states the analyzer only reports on members declared in the project being compiled. Because of the `||` in ReportIfLocatedInCompilation, this is not enforced for source locations from other compilations.

New documentation section describing the suppression policy for members of referenced types.
Global location-based filtering of all TypeCollector diagnostics (lines 239, 1436-1450), broader than fixing the indexing sites.
